newsitem.title: CHINA: Shenzhen aims at world-class bourse in 15 years.
newsitem.headline: Shenzhen aims at world-class bourse in 15 years.

text.p: The Shenzhen Stock Exchange aims to build itself into a world-class bourse in the next 15 to 20 years, with many of its services the best in China, exchange president Zhuang Xinyi was quoted on Friday as saying.

In the next 15 to 20 years, Shenzhen will "make itself rank among the world's major securities market in such areas as variety of securities, trading volume, number of listed firms, members and investors and risk control systems reaching the level of the world's advanced markets," Zhuang was quoted as saying by the China Securities newspaper.
Zhuang was making a keynote speech to a regular members' meeting of the exchange, it said.
Zhuang said the exchange aimed to build itself into the bourse with the lowest trading costs in China by using high technology.
It aims to provide the highest quality services, the best computer systems and become the best regulated market in the country, Zhuang said.
Zhuang gave no more details. China has only one other stock exchange, in Shanghai, and has no immediate plan for a third.

Analysts said Zhuang's speech was another indication that the Shenzhen exchange was making great efforts to keep up its momentum and overcome a crisis of identity over its role after China takes over Hong Kong next year. The exchange has listed 14 new foreign currency B shares with a total of 13.45 billion shares in the 18 months since the start of 1995, against Shanghai's seven firms with 6.6 billion shares.

This expansion has helped enlarge Shenzhen's B market capitalisation to around 15 billion yuan, exceeding Shanghai's 11 billion yuan. At the end of 1994, its capitalisation was only one fourth of Shanghai's.
Shenzhen has succeeded in activating the domestic A share market, overtaking Shanghai in trading volume since April.
In the five months from April to August, A share turnover in Shenzhen hit 385.9 billion yuan, against 329.9 billion yuan in Shanghai.
